steps: Boil the potatoes until a knife slides in but they are not mushy, about 3 whistles in a pressure cooker.
Let them cool fully, then peel and mash them smooth, with no lumps.
Sprinkle a little water on the poha, leave it for 5 minutes, then crush it into the potato.
Mix in the ginger, green chilli, garam masala, chaat masala, chilli powder, coriander leaves and salt.
Knead lightly into a firm dough that does not stick to your hands.
Make two balls per person and press each one into a flat round cake.
Heat the oil in a flat pan on medium, lay the tikkis in and leave them alone 2 to 3 minutes, until the base is firm and golden.
Flip gently and fry 2 to 3 minutes more until golden and crisp. Serve hot with chutney or curd.
note: A serving is now two plain tikkis, as both sources make about seven from 500 to 600 g of potato. The peas and paneer stuffing is left out to keep it an everyday snack, and poha is the binder since both sources allow it.
